steps.title: Definition
steps.body: Descriptive writing creates a vivid picture in the reader's mind using sensory details, figurative language, and careful word choices. It focuses on capturing a moment, place, or person rather than telling a story.

steps.title: Golden Rule
steps.body: Don't just describe what you see. Include sounds, smells, textures, and even tastes to bring your writing to life.

steps.title: Core Principle
steps.body: Instead of telling the reader what to feel or think, show them through specific details that allow them to experience it themselves.

steps.title: Structure Options
steps.body: Wide to narrow: Establish setting, then zoom to specific details Narrow to wide: Start with detail, then pull back to reveal context Pan across: Move through space like a camera panning

steps.title: Try it yourself
steps.body: What is the difference between descriptive writing and narrative writing? | Name three techniques for creating "show, don't tell" writing. | Why is it important to include senses beyond just sight?

steps.title: Check your answers
steps.body: Descriptive writing paints a picture of a moment or place, focusing on sensory details and atmosphere. Narrative writing tells a story with a plot, characters, and events unfolding over time. | Use sensory details, describe physical actions and reactions, include specific observations, use figurative language, focus on concrete details rather than abstract labels. | Sound, smell, touch, and taste create a more immersive experience. They trigger stronger emotional responses and memories in readers, making the description more vivid and memorable.

steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: Read the image or prompt carefully - use it as inspiration, not just description Plan your structure: viewpoint, spatial movement, key moments Use a clear viewpoint - either first person "I" or third person observer Open with impact - grab attention from the first line Balance sensory details - don't just describe visuals Vary sentence length for rhythm and effect End strongly - a final image or impression that lingers Leave time to check spelling and punctuation
